text: Fill in the blank: She ___ to school every day.
explanation: A habit uses the simple present, and a singular subject takes goes.

text: Fill in the blank: They ___ dinner when the guests arrived.
explanation: An action in progress when another happened uses the past continuous: were having.

text: Fill in the blank: I ___ him since 2015.
explanation: Since a starting point in the past calls for the present perfect: have known.

text: Fill in the blank: By the time we reached the hall, the film ___.
explanation: An action finished before another past action uses the past perfect: had started.

text: Fill in the blank: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the match.
explanation: A real condition about the future uses the present in the if-part and will in the result: will cancel.

text: Fill in the blank: She ___ for the bus for an hour before it finally came.
explanation: A long action continuing up to a past moment uses the past perfect continuous: had been waiting.

text: Fill in the blank: Neither of the boys ___ present.
explanation: Neither of takes a singular verb, so is is correct.

text: Fill in the blank: Each of the students ___ a certificate.
explanation: Each is singular, so the verb must be singular: has received.

text: Fill in the blank: The news ___ very disturbing.
explanation: News looks plural but is treated as singular, so it takes is.

text: Fill in the blank: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
explanation: The name of a subject that ends in s is still singular, so is is correct.

text: Fill in the blank: A number of students ___ absent today.
explanation: A number of means several, so the verb is plural: are.

text: Fill in the blank: The shopkeeper was fined for selling goods at a price ___ than the marked price.
explanation: The word than signals a comparison, so the comparative higher is needed.

text: Fill in the blank: She was so tired ___ she fell asleep at once.
explanation: The pattern so ... that shows a result.

text: Fill in the blank: Hardly had he reached the station ___ the train left.
explanation: Hardly is followed by when, not than.

text: Fill in the blank: No sooner did he sit down ___ the phone rang.
explanation: No sooner is followed by than, not when.
